races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden
Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who won over this course and trip on good ground 8 days ago — sole pace-setter gives him full control, though he is officially styled as a prominent runner rather than a true leader, and his chance depends entirely on whether he can sustain that lead into a steady-gallop finish.

runners_data.name: Ardeur
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a bleak recent record including two last-place finishes; 28 days off, apprentice jockey, and a sim-going record of just 1W1P from 10 — needs everything to go right from a position that is genuinely her own.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer with a recent win over 8f on good ground and strong course form; Cillian Rowan gets a handy 7lb claim and can slot in right behind Faoladh, which is exactly the position this shape rewards most.

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: Strong course record at 8f on heavy and good-to-heavy, but this 7f trip on a flat good track is marginally shorter than his best; 62 days off and Patrick McGettigan's 2lb claim doesn't fully compensate — needs a stronger pace than is likely.

runners_data.name: Rodeeve
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 6f on good ground and a genuine front-runner by nature — pushed into a midfield mapping here because so many hold-up types crowd the rear; will likely hunt a forward position regardless, which makes his price and mapping misleading.

runners_data.name: Ardadslosttheplot
runners_data.note: Compact three-year-old with placed form over this trip and trip, sitting in a natural prominent position; David Marnane's yard in form at T14:1/17, and Rebecca Parsons's 7lb claim helps off OR=68 — well placed to press Faoladh through the race.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old whose best form is over further and whose sim-going record is a concerning 13th of 15 on good ground; a natural hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield mapping in this shape, and the STYLE_FIT flag further tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Bear Right
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington three-year-old who has placed twice at 7-8f including a third at 7f on good ground last time; natural hold-up tendency but has crept into the frame before, and the Keithen Kennedy booking from a powerful yard adds interest.

runners_data.name: Prime Sign
runners_data.note: Aged five, fades in the finish according to pattern flags, and the last three runs show a consistent inability to land a blow — mapped to midfield from a natural hold-up position, and the recent run just 5 days ago adds concern about freshness.

runners_data.name: Frosted Sky
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with only three career runs, all in the 6th-8th range, and a 32-day absence; natural hold-up tendencies placed into midfield here, and the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag alongside minimal form make this a very speculative participant.

runners_data.name: Cordouan
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse whose best trip looks like 8f and who finished 9th of 25 at Hea last time; 66-day absence and the P Sweeney T14:0/2 ratio don't inspire confidence — long way to travel from the back of this field.

runners_data.name: Mehmar
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who shows consistent mid-pack finishes and whose best work comes at 5-6f rather than 7f; mapped to midfield from a hold-up base, and the Slevin yard's T14:0/1 offers little trainer momentum — limited scope to win this shape.

runners_data.name: Notforalongtime
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with placed form at this trip and course on good ground (3rd twice over 7-8f), which is more encouraging than many of her stablemates here; a natural hold-up runner remapped to midfield, and the OR=51 keeps expectations realistic despite the course form.

runners_data.name: Smaoineamh Sile
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old mare with a bleak recent record including a fall (U) last time out and a series of double-figure finishes on soft to standard; the fades-in-finish flag combined with redistribution from the rear makes this a very difficult winning proposition.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has shown flashes over 6f on good ground (3rd once) but struggles to sustain the effort over 7-8f; fades-in-finish flag, 5 days since last run, and mapped to midfield from a natural hold-up position — the Paul Flynn T14:4/25 is the only positive angle.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field, and with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead, Sam Coen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 7f trip on good ground at Leopardstown. The overwhelming majority of this field — Ardeur, God Knows, Bear Right, Ardadslosttheplot and others — are natural hold-up or off-the-pace types, meaning Faoladh sets the tempo entirely on his own terms without being pressured or forced into a suicidal early pace. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind the leader and pounce in the straight, as the steady pace is unlikely to generate the strong late gallop that pure closers depend on. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically get their natural position — Rodeeve, Frosted Sky, Dynamic Force, Prime Sign, Mehmar, Notforalongtime and Cordouan are all genuine rear-of-field runners who have been mapped to midfield on the race shape, but most will find themselves competing for the same ground late; Comfort Line and Ardadslosttheplot are best positioned to exploit a prominent berth behind the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faoladh Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh trots up uncontested and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop, allowing a prominent tracker to cruise through and collar him late.
scenarios.body: Faoladh's front-running role goes uncontested, creating a falsely-run race that rewards horses settled just off the pace with tactical reserves; Comfort Line and Ardadslosttheplot, sitting a few lengths off the leader in the slipstream, are ideally positioned to pounce inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Faoladh Bowls Along, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Sam Coen applies light pressure early and Faoladh sustains a workable gallop that proves too good for a field of closers chasing from behind.
scenarios.body: On good ground with a solo lead and a rider allowed to dictate, Faoladh can find the effort manageable and cross the line before the hold-up horses can close the gap; his recent win over this course and distance on good ground confirms the profile fits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Comes Through
scenarios.trigger: If a horse redistributed to midfield but with genuine finishing ability threads through a bunched mid-pack to emerge as the late challenger.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop causes the midfield to compress, and a horse with superior class or a strong finishing kick can navigate traffic to emerge late; Notforalongtime and Bear Right have placed form at this trip and distance that gives them a puncher's chance in this shape, though both are operating outside their most natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh runs too freely early or the pace proves entirely unsuitable, setting up a sprint finish that hands the initiative to the backmarkers.
scenarios.body: This shape requires the true hold-up horses — Ardeur, God Knows, Cordouan — to produce a sustained late surge, but many have poor recent form and are competing in a division far deeper than their finishing kicks suggest; this remains the least likely outcome given the dominant single-pace structure of the race.

watchPoints.text: Comfort Line bears watching from a prominent position — if Cillian Rowan slots in directly behind Faoladh early, the nine-year-old has the tactical profile and recent placed form to be the biggest beneficiary of a slow-run race.

Rodeeve is a natural front-runner mapped to midfield by the race shape — watch whether Adam Browne-Souza pushes forward from the stalls to claim a prominent spot, which would significantly alter the dynamic and increase pressure on Faoladh.

Ardadslosttheplot is a live danger from a prominent position if David Marnane's three-year-old settles kindly for Rebecca Parsons — the 7lb claim and recent third on good ground make her hard to dismiss if she travels smoothly behind the leader.

The clustering of hold-up horses in the midfield means traffic congestion in the final two furlongs is near-certain — horses like Bear Right and Notforalongtime may find themselves blocked at a crucial stage despite holding some form claims.

Faoladh's going record shows just two wins and four places from 15 similar-going runs despite a recent win here — if the ground has dried out beyond his comfort zone, the ability to sustain the lead into the straight may be less certain than the race shape implies.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Dublin To Bahrain Handicap

runners_data.name: Aviatrice
runners_data.note: Won twice at today's trip on standard ground, sits in good hands with Luke McAteer, and her prominent style slots perfectly into the slipstream of a single front-runner — a strong positional fit for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Loughrea
runners_data.note: Won his last two and goes well on good ground over a mile, with trainer Andrew Slattery unusually saddling his own runner — travelling prominently, he has the form to challenge once How'sthebai's advantage narrows.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up type with a visor, whose record at this distance on similar going (0W1P from 5 runs) is a significant concern — arrives just eight days after last run and needs pace to collapse for him.

runners_data.name: How'sthebai
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner for Colin Keane and G M Lyons who sets the tempo here but has zero wins or places from two runs on good going at today's trip — the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is effectively racing out of role in terms of outcome likelihood even while controlling the race.

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: Comes into this on just three days' rest with a modest recent record on good ground; genuinely a prominent type by nature, he is crowded out of that berth by stronger claims and carries the STYLE_FIT discount that tempers expectations from a displaced midfield pitch.

runners_data.name: Invincible Will
runners_data.note: Won twice at seven furlongs on good ground and shows real ability, wearing headgear and arriving fresh after only seven days — as a hold-up type he needs the pace to stack up, which is possible but not guaranteed in this controlled gallop.

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner whose best efforts came years ago; squeezed into a midfield role he doesn't want, carrying a tongue-tie and with form figures of 6-0-6-9-0 in recent starts, the value of his positional displacement to the race shape analysis is real but his chances are slim.

races.paceDynamic: How'sthebai holds the single confirmed front-running position and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will settle into a controlled, uncontested rhythm from the gates — this is a sustainable, moderate gallop rather than a pressured burn. Aviatrice and Loughrea will press from prominent positions just off the heel of How'sthebai, meaning the first few furlongs will be orderly and the pace is unlikely to fully stretch the field. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the shape can accommodate — Quatre Bras and Tachos are natural prominent racers but are mapped to midfield because How'sthebai, Aviatrice, and Loughrea are more likely to monopolise the front rank positions. A controlled pace with a bunched midfield sets up a tactical, attritional finish where horses racing prominently in the slipstream of a single front-runner are best placed — prominent types who can travel smoothly and quicken from a length or two off the leader hold the clearest positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If How'sthebai dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the race is decided by who tracks closest and quickens first inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: How'sthebai sets a comfortable tempo, Aviatrice and Loughrea sit in its slipstream and one of them kicks past as the leader ties up — a race tailor-made for horses who can travel prominently without burning energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace is so controlled that How'sthebai simply never gets headed and the prominent chasers fail to close.
scenarios.body: An uncontested lead on good ground over a mile can be a powerful weapon even for a horse racing slightly out of role, and if Colin Keane times the kick perfectly the hold-up brigade simply has too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens earlier than expected through mid-race pressure and the prominent horses burn themselves out chasing.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated gallop drags the race into truly attritional territory, creating a pocket of daylight for Invincible Will or Exquisite Acclaim to thread through late — though Exquisite Acclaim's poor record at this trip and on similar going limits confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Redistributed Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Quatre Bras or Tachos push forward from their displaced midfield positions and inject unexpected pace into the race.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their natural role and against type, both carry the [REDISTRIBUTED] and [STYLE_FIT] discounts meaning this scenario is structurally the least likely — but if either manufactures a prominent berth and disrupts the rhythm, the race becomes unpredictable and form figures count for little.

watchPoints.text: How'sthebai (Colin Keane) controls the entire pace equation — if Keane constructs an overly slow early tempo, Aviatrice and Loughrea may time their challenge too easily; watch the early fractions.

Quatre Bras (W J Lee, 3 days since last run) may attempt to reclaim his natural prominent position from the gates and push forward — if he succeeds he injects unplanned pace into the race and disrupts the scenario map.

Invincible Will (Jack Kearney, 3lb claim) is the most likely beneficiary if the race develops any pace collapse — watch his position at the two-furlong pole; if in striking range he could be dangerous.

Aviatrice (140lbs, top weight) carries the highest burden in the race — if the ground is riding firmer than expected under the unknown going report, her weight and recent prominent-running profile could tell late in the mile.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Meld Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Adelaide River
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's six-year-old has solid course-and-distance form on good ground (13 wins or places from 15 similar-going runs), and racing prominently is his natural position — the one horse other than Geryon who is likely to actually get his preferred spot in this race shape, which gives him a meaningful structural advantage.

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine hold-up type, which means McDonogh's tactics depend entirely on whether Geryon's pace is strong enough to set up a late run; good-ground form is acceptable (6 from 13 similar-going runs) but the step up from 7-8f to 1m1f is a live question given his recent starts have been over shorter.

runners_data.name: Snellen
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old carries strong overall form in good-ground conditions (15 from 15 similar-going runs), but his natural instinct to race prominently means he is likely to find himself squeezed into a midfield slot by Geryon's unchallenged lead — racing out of role tempers his chance despite the excellent going record.

runners_data.name: Syzygy
runners_data.note: Fitted with blinkers and dropping slightly in OR at 98, this four-year-old is another horse whose preference to race up with the pace will be frustrated by the race shape; good-ground form is moderate (5 from 10 similar-going runs), and being asked to race further back than ideal adds an extra layer of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Geryon
runners_data.note: G M Lyons's three-year-old is the key pace-setter here and Colin Keane will be able to control tempo without any rival threatening to take the lead; recent form shows a run of placed finishes (four seconds or fourths from last five), and while the front position gives him a tactical advantage, his finishing efforts suggest the danger is being caught rather than winning on the bridle.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old has a win over 9f on good ground to his name but also a wide variety of form positions (1st to 6th), and Wayne Lordan will find him naturally wanting to race much closer to the pace than this shape will permit — his true prominent style is the structural disadvantage here, and his best chance rests on the race producing a stronger-than-expected gallop.

races.paceDynamic: Geryon is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner Group 3 and, with no genuine rival for the lead, Colin Keane can control tempo from the front at a pace entirely of his own choosing over 1m1f on good ground at Leopardstown. This field contains more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate — Snellen, Isaac Newton, and Syzygy are all natural prominent racers who will be forced to race behind Geryon rather than alongside him, effectively becoming a compressed midfield pack. Adelaide River, racing prominently by nature, will sit closest to Geryon's quarters, while Cowardofthecounty operates from further back as the race's only genuine hold-up type. A controlled, single-file procession at a fair but unhurried pace strongly favours horses who can travel prominently, sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, and produce a finish without a dramatic gear-change — in short, horses racing in their natural position, not those who have been pushed out of it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Geryon Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Geryon dictates a measured pace unchallenged and the race is decided by sustained galloping from the front.
scenarios.body: Geryon sets a controlled tempo through the early furlongs and the race unfolds in a line, with Adelaide River the closest danger travelling just off the pace in her natural prominent position; when the tempo lifts two out, those racing in role have the advantage over the crowded midfield pack forced out of theirs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Pack Splits, One Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield contingent — Snellen, Isaac Newton, Syzygy — creates its own internal pressure and one breaks clear late.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their preferred prominent position, one of the redistributed runners manages to save enough momentum to challenge as the pace lifts from the two-furlong pole; this is against their natural grain but their class could compensate if the early gallop is truly moderate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Geryon sets a pace quick enough to stretch the field and Cowardofthecounty is produced with a well-timed late run.
scenarios.body: Declan McDonogh settles Cowardofthecounty in last and tracks the tempo; if the early fractions are genuinely strong enough to soften those in front, the hold-up horse's finishing kick could prove decisive in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If something challenges Geryon for the lead unexpectedly, lifting the tempo and turning the race into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically hot pace would scramble the race shape entirely and open the door to any horse with tactical speed or a sharp finishing burst; this is the least likely outcome given the field's composition and the absence of a confirmed challenger to Geryon's lead.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of Snellen, Isaac Newton, or Syzygy attempt to push forward early — if two or more contest the prominent positions, they could apply unexpected pressure on Geryon and inflate the early pace well beyond what a controlled lead scenario assumes.

Cowardofthecounty's chance is entirely conditional on Geryon's tempo being strong enough to set up a late run; if Keane idles in front and the pace is overly steady, McDonogh will have no race to close into from the back of this small field.

Geryon's recent form string of repeated placed efforts (2-4-4-2-4) raises a tactical flag — he has shown a pattern of being caught or pegged back when his rivals quicken, so even a pace he fully controls may not guarantee a winning finish if the prominent challengers time their challenge well.

Adelaide River's trainer Joseph O'Brien also saddles Cowardofthecounty, giving the stable a two-pronged presence; watch in the early stages whether Browne McMonagle uses Adelaide River to track Geryon closely or elects to let the pace develop before committing.

The going is listed as unknown across all reports — any late ground movement toward soft or yielding would be most significant for Syzygy, whose form markedly drops on good ground compared to easier surfaces.

races.name: Mervue Equine Handicap

runners_data.name: En Or
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with confirmed front-running intent at OR 84, last run 43 days ago; best form comes at longer trips on good ground and Ben Coen gets the ride, but jumping out in front in a race with multiple prominent rivals means the position is his to lose rather than his by right.

runners_data.name: Daler
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's booking for a four-year-old trained by G M Lyons is the headline angle here; showed a win at 9f on soft and a placed effort at 10f on good, the mile-and-two looks within range, and a prominent style means he should be travelling sweetly behind the leader from early.

runners_data.name: Unterberg
runners_data.note: A horse in fine recent form — three wins from last five including two at 12f — stepping onto turf with the caveat that his turf form (8th at 10f good) is thin; Laura Hourigan's yard is 0/2 in the last 14 days and the OR 78 rating suggests he's capable but not the standout on paper.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Five of her last five runs have come on good ground and she has placed four times in that five, making her the best going-fit runner in the race; K J Condon's yard is quiet (0/10 in 14 days) but Marmeladova's consistency as a hold-up mare who finds her way into the frame on this surface is the standout staying argument.

runners_data.name: Neo Smart
runners_data.note: A step up from sprint trips to 8f and now 10f in recent starts for Bolger, with all turf form coming on good — the trip is a question but not a disqualifier; runs out of role if he finds himself behind the pace he'd naturally want to dictate, and zero wins from two prominent runs on good turf is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has been running consistently at 10f-12f on slower ground; the good going is a genuine concern with only 4/15 similar-going runs producing results, and the 7lb claimer Joseph Harnett (7) adds an unknown tactical element over this trip.

runners_data.name: Faro Island
runners_data.note: Won twice at 10f-11f on good ground and is a naturally prominent racer — Dylan Browne McMonagle's use of him will be key — but the field's depth of prominent types means he is unlikely to secure his preferred berth just off the leader, which is the honest reason his chance is discounted here.

runners_data.name: Out On Friday
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old who twice found the frame at 10f on good going but carries a clear "fades in finish" flag and sits at OR 65; amateur claim by Wesley Joyce (3) is a factor, and at this age needing things to fall perfectly makes him a very conditional participant.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: Two wins to his name (on Flat and AW) but the most recent turf form at Leopardstown's trip shows 7th and well-beaten efforts; a genuine hold-up horse who also carries the "fades in finish" flag — the redistribution to midfield in the map reflects crowding at the rear rather than a change in how Robbie Colgan will ride him, and the STYLE_FIT discount is warranted.

races.paceDynamic: En Or is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press from the outside, should be able to roll along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this mile-and-two on good turf at Leopardstown. Daler, Unterberg, and Neo Smart all carry prominent profiles but with En Or already committed to the lead, at least one of them will be squeezed into a position slightly further back than ideal, softening the pace pressure on the leader. The field does hold more naturally prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Faro Island is a genuine front-of-the-field racer pushed into a midfield mapping, and Blackjack Hills is a true hold-up horse shown in midfield due to clustering at the rear — meaning the actual pace picture is marginally more compressed than the chart suggests. A leader allowed to dictate at a measured tempo over a distance that suits stamina profiles is the dominant scenario here, and the race shape therefore favours horses who can sit just off a genuine but unhurried gallop and produce a sustained rather than explosive late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If En Or is allowed to roll along unchallenged and the prominent trio fail to apply meaningful pressure through the middle mile.
scenarios.body: En Or dictates a measured tempo and, with no rival forcing a genuine injection of pace, the lead never becomes truly vulnerable until the final furlong; horses who can sit a length or two off the pace and grind rather than sprint home are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Leader Down
scenarios.trigger: If Daler or Unterberg apply sustained pressure on En Or from the half-mile pole, lifting the tempo into the straight.
scenarios.body: The race develops into a genuine stamina test as En Or is pressed before the final turn, and the horse who has sat just off the contested lead emerges strongest; Colin Keane's tactical read on Daler through the middle stages becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the front group ties each other up, creating a race into which a hold-up horse can deliver a meaningful late run.
scenarios.body: Marmeladova, with the best recent good-going form figures in the field and a habit of finding the line under W J Lee, is the chief beneficiary; Sinbad My Dad offers each-way interest if the fractions are truly testing and the field spreads across the track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Pace Shape
scenarios.trigger: If prominent types jostle for position early and a falsely run race produces an unpredictable finish from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A scrambled tempo with multiple horses failing to settle in their preferred spots would suit a horse with tactical versatility like Faro Island — genuinely prominent in reality but capable of adjusting — though the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence; Out On Friday would need everything to fall right at age ten.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of Daler, Unterberg, or Neo Smart presses En Or early — if two of the three prominent types push for position in the first quarter-mile, the tempo could be falsely fast and undermine the leader's hold on proceedings.
Marmeladova's trainer Condon is 0/10 in the last 14 days; if she is held up as usual and the race is run at a muddling pace rather than a genuine test, her late run may not arrive in time to matter.

Faro Island is ridden by the in-form Dylan Browne McMonagle but the horse's natural position is at the front of the field — watch at the start to see whether he is restrained or allowed to find his own ground, as that decision will shape whether his true ability is expressed.

Out On Friday at age ten and OR 65 is a situational runner only — his last competitive finish was a place at 10f good, but the "fades in finish" flag means any apparent travelling well in the straight should be treated with caution before the final furlong.

Blackjack Hills has wins on AW and soft/heavy equivalents but turf-on-good form is limited and declining — monitor early market moves, as a drift would confirm that connections share the concern about the surface conditions.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap

runners_data.name: Ob La Di
runners_data.note: Best RPR in the field at 80, Ben Coen booked for J P Murtagh's 5-year-old who has fair good-ground form at 1m2f but steps up to 1m5f here — the extra trip is an open question, and her deep hold-up style means she needs a genuinely strong pace to make an impact.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, lightly weighted on OR 71, but ran just five days ago and the quick turnaround under Robbie Colgan is worth noting; her headgear (p) is retained and she has winning form on standard going — the key is whether recent exertion blunts her resolve over this longer 1m5f trip.

runners_data.name: Killyclogher Rose
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 1m3f last time for A Oliver and W J Lee, and steps up to 1m5f for the first time — she is a prominent tracker by style and her recent winning form makes her the most dangerous threat to the leader if the trip is within range.

runners_data.name: Derry Lad
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old held up on a tp mark with a clear flag on his tendency to fade in the finish, and his recent form string of 99055 signals a horse struggling for consistency; Colin Keane takes the ride but there are few positives in this profile at this trip.

runners_data.name: Tatum
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner by nature and a winner twice on good ground at middle-distance trips — Dylan Browne McMonagle is an excellent booking, but the horse holds a blinkers entry and is inevitably going to race out of his natural position given the pace situation, which tempers confidence despite his solid form credentials.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners this 4-year-old who has placed twice on good ground but has yet to win on it; she is a natural front-runner squeezed out of her preferred position in this field, and without the ability to stride on from the front her best form looks hard to replicate.

races.paceDynamic: Cala Bonita is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival likely to seriously contest early supremacy over this 1m5f trip, she should be able to dictate at a comfortable, controlled tempo from the front. Killyclogher Rose is the most credible prominent threat but rates as a tracker rather than a challenger for the lead, meaning Cala Bonita gets an uncontested lead and sets a pace entirely on her own terms. This field does contain more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate — Tatum and Cooley's Mist are genuine front-running or prominent types by nature but are mapped to midfield because the prominent berths are already filled, meaning both will likely race in an unnatural position. A sustainable, front-dictated pace over a staying trip on good ground favours horses who can track the leader closely and produce a decisive finish, giving the edge to prominent-to-midfield types with strong form at this distance range rather than deep closers who will need the pace to truly collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cala Bonita Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Cala Bonita leads unchallenged from the outset and sets a steady-to-fair gallop that never allows closers to build momentum.
scenarios.body: Cala Bonita dictates every yard, conserving enough energy through the relatively flat middle stages to fight off challengers from the home turn, and Killyclogher Rose, positioned just behind, is ideally placed to pounce if the leader tires late. The controlled tempo over 1m5f suits horses racing prominently with strong staying form, putting Killyclogher Rose and Cala Bonita firmly in the firing line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and the closers get a strong enough gallop to reel in the front-runner in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ob La Di, the most natural hold-up horse in the field with solid good-ground form, would benefit most if Cala Bonita over-commits early and leaves her vulnerable to a late challenge. Derry Lad could factor in this shape though his tendency to fade in the finish is a significant concern.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Get Box Seat
scenarios.trigger: If Tatum or Cooley's Mist manage to push forward and secure a prominent position closer to their natural style than their mapped position suggests.
scenarios.body: Both horses are temperamentally front-running types forced into mid-division, so if the early pace is sedated enough they could edge forward and race on the premises — Tatum, who has won twice on good ground at this sort of trip, would be the chief beneficiary with Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle. Cooley's Mist lacks the winning form profile to capitalise even in an ideal scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Early Pace Test
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses press Cala Bonita hard early, turning this into a genuinely searching test of stamina that burns off the front-runner.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early gallop would collapse the field into a stamina-sapping finish where Ob La Di's hold-up style and better RPR could prove decisive, and Tatum's proven winning form at 1m3f-1m5f on good ground gives him residual claims. This scenario is the least likely given Cala Bonita's uncontested status and the natural order of this field.

watchPoints.text: Cala Bonita ran just five days ago — watch closely in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of flatness or reluctance to go forward, as her entire race plan depends on sustained front-running over a longer trip than she has recently tackled.

Tatum and Cooley's Mist may both attempt to push forward off the break despite being mapped to midfield — if either succeeds in challenging Cala Bonita early, the pace dynamic changes significantly and closers like Ob La Di come into sharper focus.
Killyclogher Rose is unproven beyond 1m3f — if the pace is slow and the race develops into a sprint finish, her stamina for the extra furlong of 1m5f becomes the decisive unknown in her chance.

Ob La Di has finished in the top five in three of her last four runs on good ground at around a mile but has been beaten by considerable margins — watch whether Ben Coen switches tactics and makes an earlier move than her natural hold-up style would suggest given the moderate pace likely on offer.
